highlights.title: No reduced motion support
highlights.detail: Implement prefers-reduced-motion to allow users to disable animations, reducing compute and improving accessibility.

criteria.title: Control animation
criteria.description: Allow users to start, stop, pause, or otherwise control animated content.

guideline.title: Ensure animation is proportionate and easy to control
guideline.subheading: Ensure any animation deemed necessary is not overdone and that the user can control its ability to run.

benefits.Environment: Disabling and reducing animation to the essential, with appropriate optimization and user control, reduces rendering impact and associated emissions.
benefits.Performance: Compressing, removing, or otherwise reducing animation files reduces complexity, improving performance.
benefits.Social Equity: Catering to different perspectives on and preferences in relation to animation can improve acceptance and access for individuals using different devices and from different backgrounds.

highlights.title: Review User Journey Efficiency
highlights.detail: Have a human walk through the main user journeys and verify they require the fewest steps possible. Unnecessary steps waste user time and device energy. Look for redundant confirmations, forced account creation, and non-essential interstitials.

highlights.title: Check for Engagement Traps
highlights.detail: Manually review the page for patterns that artificially prolong engagement: infinite scroll, autoplay carousels, sticky overlays, and notification permission prompts. These waste user attention and device energy.

highlights.title: Audit for Deceptive Design Patterns
highlights.detail: Have a human identify dark patterns: misleading consent dialogs, hidden unsubscribe links, forced continuity, and bait-and-switch flows. Deceptive patterns waste user time and undermine trust.

highlights.title: Verify Accessible Alternatives for All Media
highlights.detail: Manually check that every video has captions, every audio file has a transcript, every image has meaningful alt text, and every PDF has an accessible HTML alternative. Alternatives let assistive technology users avoid re-downloading heavy formats.

highlights.title: Confirm User Research Was Conducted
highlights.detail: Verify that genuine user research or usability testing has informed the design. Research-driven design reduces wasted iterations, removes unnecessary features, and ensures the product meets real needs efficiently.

highlights.title: Review Content Conciseness
highlights.detail: Use a Large Language Model to evaluate page text for conciseness and clarity. Removing superfluous text reduces payload, reading time, and inference energy for search engines and AI crawlers indexing this content.

highlights.title: Evaluate Navigation and Wayfinding Quality
highlights.detail: Ask an LLM to assess whether the navigation labels, headings, and page hierarchy allow a user to locate content in as few steps as possible. Poor information architecture forces repeat page loads and increases server and user energy costs.

highlights.title: Evaluate HTML Semantic Correctness
highlights.detail: Use an LLM or structured analysis tool to verify that HTML uses semantic elements (article, nav, main, section, aside) correctly. Proper semantics reduces duplicate markup, improves accessibility, and allows browsers and crawlers to process pages more efficiently.

highlights.title: Verify Error Pages and Redirects Are Configured
highlights.detail: Have a human check that custom 404 and 500 error pages exist and that there are no redirect chains longer than one hop. Broken links force wasted round-trips. Redirect chains multiply transfer costs.

highlights.title: Review CDN Usage and Geographic Distribution
highlights.detail: Confirm that static assets are served from a CDN and that the CDN edge nodes are geographically close to the primary audience. CDN misuse—or absence—increases last-mile transfer distance and the associated energy cost of data delivery.

highlights.title: Confirm a Sustainability Advocate Is Assigned
highlights.detail: Verify that someone on the team has explicit responsibility for web sustainability. Without a designated advocate, sustainability improvements tend to be deprioritized and never reach the backlog.

highlights.title: Check for a Public Sustainability Statement
highlights.detail: Look for a publicly accessible sustainability statement, disclosure page, or environmental policy. Mandatory disclosure requirements are growing globally and transparency builds user trust. The statement should include measurable targets and dates.

## Improve Reduce unused JavaScript

- Lighthouse audit: unused-javascript
- Current value: Est savings of 26 KiB
- WSG guideline: 16 Use dependencies appropriately and ensure maintenance
- WSG link: https://www.w3.org/TR/web-sustainability-guidelines/#use-dependencies-appropriately-and-ensure-maintenance

### Why this matters
Reduce unused JavaScript and defer loading scripts until they are required to decrease bytes consumed by network activity. [Learn how to reduce unused JavaScript](https://developer.chrome.com/docs/lighthouse/performance/unused-javascript/).

### Definition of done
- [ ] Metric improves in Lighthouse on key templates
- [ ] Changes documented in release notes
- [ ] Re-scan confirms improvement
